To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmeretail.com
Date: Tue, 25 Apr 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on mini-invoice floor for our short-context flows

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Acme's product team liked the latency profile. Before we move into the pilot, procurement flagged a billing question we need cleared up: many of our calls are tiny (50–120 token exchanges, often single-turn lookups). With the proposed pricing, how will the mini-invoice floor / quantum interact with short calls?

Concrete example: if a user triggers a lookup that yields a 40-token prompt + 60-token response, does that count as 100 tokens billed, or do you apply any minimum quantum (e.g., 128-token minimum per call) that would round up? Also curious whether context-length (max context) impacts rounding separately from per-call quantum.

Procurement is worried about the pilot appearing expensive relative to expected token volumes. Can you send a sample mini-invoice that shows the floor applied across a week of small calls? I've attached a tiny sample of our expected call distribution (AcmePilot_Metrics.xlsx).

Appreciate a quick clarification so we can finalize the PO.

— Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Integrations, Acme Retail
liam.oconnor@acmeretail.com
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Questions on mini-invoice floor for our short-context flows

Liam,

Thanks for the clear example — helpful. Short answer: billing combines two things that can affect the numbers you see: the per-request quantum (we bill in fixed token increments for meterability) and a per-request minimum that prevents micro-invoice noise. A few bullet points to make this concrete: 

- Token accounting: we count input + output tokens (your 40 + 60 = 100 tokens).
- Quantum & rounding: by default we meter to the nearest 64-token quantum per request (so 100 tokens would round up to 128 tokens billed).
- Minimums/mini-invoice: for hosted plans we also apply a micro-request floor of 64 tokens for any request under the quantum window; on Dedicated this floor is usually disabled. Essentially your 100-token call would be billed as 128 tokens in the standard hosted pricing path.
- Context length: the model window (max context) impacts whether we need model-surgery/tiling, but does not change the quantum; it only affects how we split long requests.

That said, we frequently make pilot concessions for telemetry-heavy customers doing lots of tiny calls — e.g., temporary removal of the micro-invoice floor for the pilot or a deposit/credit that offsets the rounding noise. I've sketched a sample week invoice against your attached histogram to show the delta (attachment).

Call out: if you can do lightweight prefix caching (same 10–20 token prefix across calls), the effective billed tokens drop further because cached prefixes aren't re-tokenized on every call. We can help you instrument that during onboarding.

I'll loop in our pricing lead internally and propose a pilot concession you can present to procurement.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Apr 2028 10:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mini-invoice floor for Acme pilot — suggested concession

Irene / Ben,

Quick internal note on what we can offer to close HS-6721: 

- Proposal A (preferred): Waive the micro-invoice floor (the 64-token mini floor) for the first 90 days of the pilot. We keep the quantum metering (64-token increments) but don't apply the additional per-request floor credit. We show the week-by-week projected invoice delta in redwood_pricing_concession_v1.pdf.
- Proposal B: Keep floor, but provide a fixed weekly credit equal to the estimated rounding delta based on their histogram (simple to operationalize via client credits).
- Operational ask: Acme wants line-iteming on the mini-invoice so procurement can see per-request rounding deltas. We can provide CSV-level invoice exports for the pilot.

Ben — can you confirm impact on our hosted billing pipeline and whether ops needs a manual flag to flip for 90 days? I think this is doable without product changes but need ops signoff. Also suggest we append a clause in the pilot SOW that says rounding concessions are promotional and will revert to standard metering after the pilot unless we agree to a committed volume.

-Vanessa
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 27 Apr 2028 16:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on mini-invoice floor for our short-context flows

Liam — thanks for the patience. Following internal check-ins here is a concise concession we can put in the pilot SOW: 

1) 90-day pilot concession: Redwood will waive the micro-invoice floor for all hosted requests originating from Acme's pilot API key for 90 days starting on pilot go-live. We will continue to meter in 64-token quanta (requests will still round up to the nearest 64-token quantum), but we will not apply the additional per-request mini-floor credit during that window.

2) Accounting visibility: we'll provide a CSV export showing per-request token counts, pre-rounding and post-rounding billed tokens, and a weekly rollup that isolates the rounding delta so procurement can reconcile.

3) Pilot cap & credit: to protect Redwood from extreme abuse while we waive the floor, we ask for a $3,000 pilot cap payable in advance; any unused portion will be credited against first paid month. 

Attached is a one-page worked example using your distribution (AcmePilot_Metrics.xlsx) and a redwood_pricing_concession_v1.pdf that shows projected invoice comparisons (floor vs. waived). If you like this path we can add the concession language into the SOW and route to signatures (DocuSign link can be generated once you confirm).

Let me know if procurement needs different formatting for the sample invoice. Happy to hop on a short call to walk through the CSV columns.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
